patterns.label: appeal_to_authority
patterns.definition: A source's status substitutes for adequate justification of a claim. Identify source, asserted claim and the authority-to-truth step. A named example or qualified testimony is not automatically fallacious; do not infer incompetence from missing citations.
patterns.mechanism: A source's status substitutes for adequate justification of a claim. Identify source, asserted claim and the authority-to-truth step. A named example or qualified testimony is not automatically fallacious; do not infer incompetence from missing citations.
patterns.logical_form: Person/Source P asserts claim C -> Therefore C is true (without domain-relevant empirical justification).
cue_examples: According to [expert/celebrity/title]...
Listen to the experts instead of questioning...
Dr./Professor X said that...
Citing prestige or official status as the sole verification.

criteria.statement: A source or person is offered as warrant for a claim.
The source status substitutes for adequate justification of the conclusion.
The target relies on qualified testimony with relevant evidence rather than status as a substitute.

patterns.label: appeal_to_majority
patterns.definition: Popularity or widespread acceptance is used to establish truth or correctness. Identify the popular belief and the conclusion it supposedly proves. Describing opinion or preferences for a legitimate decision does not by itself establish this defect.
patterns.mechanism: Popularity or widespread acceptance is used to establish truth or correctness. Identify the popular belief and the conclusion it supposedly proves. Describing opinion or preferences for a legitimate decision does not by itself establish this defect.
patterns.logical_form: Group G (everyone, majority, X% of people) believes/endorses claim C -> Therefore C is valid/true.
cue_examples: Everyone knows that...
Most people agree that...
51% of people believe...
It can't be that the entire world is wrong...
No one believes that anymore...
Appealing to popular vote or consensus as factual proof.

criteria.statement: Popularity or widespread acceptance is invoked.
Popularity is used to establish truth or correctness.
The target only describes preferences, opinion or a legitimate collective decision.
The inference instead generalizes from limited cases to a population.

patterns.label: appeal_to_nature
patterns.definition: Naturalness or artificiality is used to establish value, safety or correctness without an adequate bridge. Identify that value inference, not a mere biological description.
patterns.mechanism: Naturalness or artificiality is used to establish value, safety or correctness without an adequate bridge. Identify that value inference, not a mere biological description.
patterns.logical_form: X is natural -> Therefore X is good/safe/healthy; or Y is artificial/unnatural -> Therefore Y is bad/harmful.
cue_examples: It's all-natural, so it's completely safe/healthy...
Unnatural chemicals / against nature...
Nature intended it this way...
Equating artificial or processed with inherently destructive or immoral.

criteria.statement: Naturalness or artificiality is invoked.
Value, safety or correctness is inferred from naturalness without an adequate bridge.
The target offers specific empirical evidence rather than naturalness as the warrant.

patterns.label: appeal_to_tradition
patterns.definition: Longevity or customary practice is used to establish correctness or a requirement to preserve a practice. Historical background or affection alone is insufficient.
patterns.mechanism: Longevity or customary practice is used to establish correctness or a requirement to preserve a practice. Historical background or affection alone is insufficient.
patterns.logical_form: Practice/Belief X has been done for a long time / is traditional -> Therefore X is correct, optimal, or right.
cue_examples: We have always done it this way...
Time-tested tradition proves...
Centuries of custom dictate that...
Traditional values must be maintained because of history.

criteria.statement: Longevity or customary practice is invoked.
Historical persistence is used to establish correctness or the need to preserve the practice.
The target provides historical background or affection without a justificatory inference.

patterns.label: appeal_to_worse_problems
patterns.definition: A distinguishable, allegedly more serious problem B is used to dismiss or defer concern A without a supplied justification for that dismissal. A and B may be related. Identify both concerns and the dismissal; a warranted resource tradeoff is not enough.
patterns.mechanism: A distinguishable, allegedly more serious problem B is used to dismiss or defer concern A without a supplied justification for that dismissal. A and B may be related. Identify both concerns and the dismissal; a warranted resource tradeoff is not enough.
patterns.logical_form: Issue X is raised; Separate Problem Y exists where Severity(Y) > Severity(X) -> Therefore dismiss/ignore X.
cue_examples: Why are we worrying about X when people are dying of Y?
There are far worse problems in the world than X...
First solve Y before complaining about X...
What about [greater external catastrophe]?

criteria.statement: A distinguishable allegedly more serious problem B is introduced beside concern A.
The severity of B is used to dismiss or defer A without supplied justification.
The target instead predicts escalation from A itself.
The comparison expresses a justified resource tradeoff rather than dismissal.

patterns.label: false_dilemma
patterns.definition: An explicit or textually licensed implicit exhaustiveness commitment excludes relevant alternatives. Identify the restricted options and the commitment; two options need not be enumerated. Do not invent an option merely to create a binary. Recommendations alone do not suffice.
patterns.mechanism: An explicit or textually licensed implicit exhaustiveness commitment excludes relevant alternatives. Identify the restricted options and the commitment; two options need not be enumerated. Do not invent an option merely to create a binary. Recommendations alone do not suffice.
patterns.logical_form: Premise: Either A or B (A OR B; NOT A -> B), falsely asserting exhaustiveness -> Therefore choose A or B.
cue_examples: Either A or B, there is no other way...
You're either with us or against us...
Pick a side / you must choose between X and Y...
The only alternative to X is total Y...
No middle ground.

criteria.statement: The target commits explicitly or implicitly to restricted exhaustive alternatives.
The restriction excludes relevant alternatives without warrant.
The alternatives are genuinely exhaustive or no exhaustiveness is committed.
The defect instead concerns an unsupported causal escalation.

patterns.label: hasty_generalization
patterns.definition: A limited or unrepresentative case/sample is used to infer a broader population or class claim. Identify case, generalized scope and the leap. The generalization may be intermediate, not the final recommendation. Broad assertions alone do not suffice.
patterns.mechanism: A limited or unrepresentative case/sample is used to infer a broader population or class claim. Identify case, generalized scope and the leap. The generalization may be intermediate, not the final recommendation. Broad assertions alone do not suffice.
patterns.logical_form: Limited/anecdotal subset S (subset of A) exhibits property P -> Therefore all A exhibits property P.
cue_examples: I know someone who... therefore all of them...
In my personal experience, so it always happens...
I saw one instance, which proves everyone...
Universal quantifiers (always, never, everyone, nobody) derived from anecdotes.

criteria.statement: A limited case or unrepresentative sample is offered.
A broader population or class conclusion is inferred from those cases.
The sample-to-population leap lacks sufficient justification.
The statement is a broad assertion with no sample-to-population inference.
Popularity itself, rather than a limited sample, is used as proof.

patterns.label: slippery_slope
patterns.definition: An action/event is claimed to produce an unwarranted escalation, progression or loss of a stopping boundary. Identify the actual transition(s) and the unsupported escalation commitment. A negative forecast, future tense, severity or "can lead to" alone is insufficient. Do not invent intermediate events or strengthen possibility into inevitability.
patterns.mechanism: An action/event is claimed to produce an unwarranted escalation, progression or loss of a stopping boundary. Identify the actual transition(s) and the unsupported escalation commitment. A negative forecast, future tense, severity or "can lead to" alone is insufficient. Do not invent intermediate events or strengthen possibility into inevitability.
patterns.logical_form: A occurs -> Inevitable negative deterioration or escalation (B, or B -> ... -> Z) without sufficient causal warrants.
cue_examples: If we allow A, next will be B, and eventually Z...
A dangerous precedent / opens the floodgates / can lead to...
Where does it end? / What is next? / Who else is next?
Things will only get worse / things just get bad / if nothing is done / otherwise...

criteria.statement: An action or event is linked to a progression, escalation or loss of a stopping boundary.
The projected progression moves toward more severe outcomes.
The target passage asserts an escalation transition without an adequate causal bridge.
The target instead uses a distinct worse concern to dismiss the current concern.
The target only offers a negative forecast without an escalation commitment.
